speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) over the last 10 years, what has been the trend of Singaporeans being declared bankrupt; (b) what is the average time taken to exit bankruptcy; and (c) what are the measures taken to ease difficulties in job search and employment because of bankruptcy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Ministry of Law has introduced various enhancements to the bankruptcy regime to help individuals avoid bankruptcy and also reduce the time taken for bankrupts to exit bankruptcy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will allow more debtors to qualify for DRS and avoid bankruptcy with the consequent risk of losing their jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Differentiated Discharge Framework (DDF), which was introduced in 2016, provides a more rehabilitative regime, with clear goals and timelines for the insolvent individual to meet to be discharged at various points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For cases which pre-date DDF, the Insolvency Office has since 2014 stepped up efforts to actively review deserving bankruptcy cases for a timely discharge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Individual bankrupts who have made satisfactory contributions to their estate and who have been cooperative with the Insolvency Office during the administration of their bankruptcy are discharged expeditiously, so that they can have a fresh start in their financial affairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Insolvency Office routinely advises Singaporean bankrupts who require assistance on employment on the available avenues for help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such avenues include Workforce Singapore (WSG) and the National Trades Union Congress' Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: And through the Adapt and Grow initiative, WSG and e2i offer employment facilitation services, such as career coaching, employability workshops, job fairs and job matching.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: They also provide a suite of employment support programmes to help jobseekers, including bankrupts, take up new jobs and careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: All employers in Singapore are expected to practise fair and merit-based employment practices, as laid out in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This may be necessary for some jobs, for example, those in the financial industry, where employees are required to be free from any financial embarrassment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One, increasingly, Singaporeans would need to travel to seek employment opportunities outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How prepared are we to allow Singaporeans who are bankrupts to make regular travels so that they can establish a career and so that they can eventually pay off their debts?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second point is, as we head towards economic uncertainty, how flexible is the system to prevent more Singaporeans who get into bankruptcy or to get out of bankruptcy faster, so that they can latch on to better opportunities?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It minimises and mitigates the risks of any dissipation of assets or any leakage in terms of the bankrupt's estate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Member's second question is about the flexibility of the framework.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I explained in my opening remarks and the answer I gave earlier, we are looking at different options, both before bankruptcy as well as the differentiated framework after bankruptcy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That allows the Official Assignee to look at circumstances relevant to the particular bankrupt, as the case may be, for the purposes of this charge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Obviously, the conduct and the affairs of the estate for two bankrupts will not be the same.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, those factors will be looked at in terms of the differentiated discharge framework.
